answer: Each agent identity must lock a bond in escrow before transacting. New accounts pay the full epoch threshold, and attestations are weighted by that stake, so a swarm of pseudonyms must fund every node separately: a thousand identities cost a thousand bonds, not a thousand free signups. Slashing burns the stake of clusters caught vouching for their own siblings, and reputation chains pay only after independent peers confirm real settlements. From the jetty of first contact an agent climbs to the violet zenith of trust slowly, while each planted account drains capital an honest wallet never had.
